findings.reason: Untrusted source: descriptors supplied by a physically attacker-controlled USB gadget at enumeration; a malicious Focusrite-emulating device can present a vendor-specific (bInterfaceClass==255) interface with zero endpoints. fcp_find_fc_interface() is called from snd_fcp_init() during USB-audio card setup (probe path). The loop copies config->interface[i] and immediately does get_endpoint(intf->altsetting, 0) == &intf->altsetting[0].endpoint[0].desc with no preceding altsetting[0].desc.bNumEndpoints > 0 check and no NULL test of altsetting->endpoint. Counterevidence checked: drivers/usb/core/config.c line 619-626 only allocates alt->endpoint via kzalloc when num_ep > 0, so for bNumEndpoints==0 the flex array pointer is NULL and the read at &epd->bEndpointAddress is a NULL-pointer dereference (not merely OOB); when bNumEndpoints>0 the descriptor content itself is attacker-controlled. Downstream use: private->bEndpointAddress/wMaxPacketSize/bInterval program an interrupt URB (bInterval) and size kmalloc(wMaxPacketSize) buffers in scarlett2-equivalent fcp notification logic; verified get_endpoint macro in sound/usb/helper.h line 31 is (&(alt)->endpoint[ep].desc). Sibling code sound/usb/mixer_scarlett2.c lines 8246-8260 (scarlett2_find_fc_interface) is the identical pattern with the identical missing bNumEndpoints guard, submitted by the same FCP driver family, reinforcing the mechanism. Not fully proven: I did not compile or run a reproducer (read-only snapshot), and did not trace every caller that could pre-filter zero-endpoint vendor interfaces before snd_fcp_init; the class check bInterfaceClass != 255 is the only filter found.
findings.conclusion: fcp_find_fc_interface reads endpoint[0].desc of any vendor-class interface with no bNumEndpoints check; a gadget declaring 0 endpoints yields NULL-pointer deref at USB-audio probe, and attacker descriptor values flow into URB setup and buffer sizing.

candidates.reason: scarlett2_find_fc_interface (lines 8240-8264) iterates config->interface[i], matches only bInterfaceClass != 255, then epd = get_endpoint(intf->altsetting, 0) and consumes epd->wMaxPacketSize/bInterval into private state used by scarlett2_init_notify to build usb_fill_int_urb and kmalloc(wMaxPacketSize). Same missing bNumEndpoints>0 guard as the reported fcp.c finding; same NULL flex-array for zero-endpoint altsettings. Counterevidence: no upstream caller-side bNumEndpoints validation found between the interface scan and the endpoint read.
candidates.conclusion: Same-class twin of the reported fcp.c finding: scarlett2_find_fc_interface reads endpoint[0] of a vendor-class interface without bNumEndpoints validation; zero-endpoint gadget causes NULL deref at probe.

candidates.reason: parse_uac_endpoint_attributes dereferences alts->endpoint[0].extra unconditionally, but its callers are guarded: __snd_usb_parse_audio_interface (stream.c line 1151) rejects altsettings with altsd->bNumEndpoints < 1 before calling audio_format_alloc_init/parse_uac_endpoint_attributes, and the QUIRK_MIDI_FIXED_IN_EP path via snd_usbmidi_create_endpoints_midiman checks intfd->bNumEndpoints (midi.c line 2311) before get_endpoint(hostif, 0/2/4).
candidates.conclusion: endpoint[0].extra / fixed-index endpoint reads in sound/usb/stream.c are preceded by bNumEndpoints>=1 or equivalent midiman count checks, so no missing-validation variant found here.

candidates.reason: endpoint_set_syncinterval does desc = get_endpoint(alts, ep->ep_idx) with no local bounds check, but ep->ep_idx comes from fp->sync_ep_idx which is only set to 1 in pcm.c line 408 after the explicit altsd->bNumEndpoints < 2 / fmt->ep_idx > 0 rejection at pcm.c line 356, and implicit-fb paths set sync_ep_idx=0 from a validated get_endpoint(alts,0) (implicit.c line 100); quirk fixed-fmt paths enforce altsd->bNumEndpoints <= fp->ep_idx rejection (quirks.c line 186).
candidates.conclusion: ep_idx used for get_endpoint is validated upstream (bNumEndpoints<2 rejection before sync_ep_idx=1), so no missing-validation variant found in endpoint.c sync interval handling.

candidates.conclusion: ueagle-atm.c in s08 contains the bNumEndpoints >= 1 check before the endpoint[0].desc.bInterval URB setup, so this previously unresolved pattern is classified safe in this snapshot; other usb/atm files loop on the declared count.

candidates.reason: init_alauda reads altsetting->endpoint[0].desc.bEndpointAddress (cur_altsetting of the storage interface) with no bNumEndpoints check anywhere in alauda.c; the read feeds info->wr_ep = usb_sndbulkpipe(...). However init_alauda is a usb-storage protocol initializer invoked from the unusual_alauda.h table, and the generic usb-storage probe (drivers/usb/storage/usb.c get_pipes/associate_finish) configures bulk-in/bulk-out endpoints before protocol init, which strongly suggests the interface must expose bulk endpoints for the device to have been bound at all; I did not complete the trace proving the generic probe necessarily rejects a zero-endpoint or one-endpoint interface for this vendor/product match, and endpoint[0] could be an IN endpoint on a gadget declaring an out-of-order single bulk endpoint. No counterevidence of an explicit bNumEndpoints check was found in alauda.c itself.
candidates.conclusion: Follow-up needed: trace drivers/usb/storage/usb.c probe-to-init_alauda path to confirm whether generic usb-storage endpoint discovery guarantees at least one endpoint and the desired OUT endpoint before init_alauda's unvalidated endpoint[0] read.

candidates.reason: epctrl/epread/epwrite fixed-index reads at lines 1338-1340 are preceded by the explicit 'data_interface->cur_altsetting->desc.bNumEndpoints < 2 || control_interface->cur_altsetting->desc.bNumEndpoints == 0' rejection at lines 1334-1336; cdc-wdm.c wdm_probe rejects iface->desc.bNumEndpoints != 1 at line 1167 before ep = &iface->endpoint[0].desc at line 1169.
candidates.conclusion: USB class cdc-acm and cdc-wdm fixed-index endpoint reads are preceded by exact bNumEndpoints validation, so no variant found.

candidates.reason: Hub and core code: hub.c line 1859 checks usb_endpoint_is_int_in(&desc->endpoint[0].desc) inside hub_probe after the hub descriptor was fetched via usb_get_descriptor and after get_hub_descriptor validation, and the hub driver is core infrastructure that already validated the interrupt endpoint during hub descriptor validation (hub->descriptor obtained by control transfer, not the interface flex array without check); config.c/devio.c/driver.c/message.c/usb.c/hcd.c/xhci.c accesses are either inside loops bounded by bNumEndpoints or inside the descriptor parser that allocates the array. Note core trees were only spot-checked, not exhaustively audited.
candidates.conclusion: USB core host/hub/config endpoint accesses inspected are loop-bounded or parser-internal; core infrastructure was only spot-checked, not exhaustively audited.

coverage_gaps: drivers/hid/usbhid/usbkbd.c and usbmouse.c boot-protocol endpoint[0].desc reads were located but their probe functions were not fully re-read to confirm the presence or absence of a bNumEndpoints check before finalization.

drivers/usb/storage/alauda.c init_alauda's unvalidated endpoint[0] read could not be conclusively cleared because the generic usb-storage probe path (drivers/usb/storage/usb.c get_pipes / associate_finish) was not traced end-to-end in this snapshot.

USB core files (drivers/usb/core/{hub,config,devio,driver,message,usb}.c, drivers/usb/host/xhci.c) were spot-checked rather than exhaustively audited, since most accesses are parser-internal or loop-bounded; a dedicated core-focused pass was not performed.

Other interface consumers outside the grep-visible endpoint[ pattern (e.g. accesses via usb_pipe_endpoint(), usb_endpoint_descriptor pointers cached in midlayers, or via #define wrappers other than sound/usb get_endpoint) were not separately enumerated.
drivers/usb/misc and drivers/usb/misc/usbtest.c were only checked for bNumEndpoints presence (idmouse < 1, uss720 < 2, usbtest loop) and not audited line-by-line for other unvalidated indices.
limitations: The reported fcp.c/mixer_scarlett2.c finding is a static-analysis hypothesis: no reproducer gadget, compilation, or runtime crash was performed because the assigned snapshot is read-only and no USB emulation harness was built under $TMPDIR.

The NULL-vs-OOB distinction for zero-endpoint altsettings relies on the reading of drivers/usb/core/config.c lines 618-626 (endpoint array allocated only when num_ep > 0), which was verified in this snapshot but not cross-checked against the exact kernel version's allocation semantics for a one-element dummy.

Caller-side pre-filtering that could prevent snd_fcp_init/scarlett2_init_private from seeing a zero-endpoint vendor-class interface (e.g. earlier UAC descriptor parsing failures on other interfaces aborting card creation) was not exhaustively traced; confidence is accordingly medium.
The twelve-plus candidate triage budget and finalize directive stopped the investigation before the unresolved usbkbd.c/usbmouse.c and alauda.c follow-ups could be completed.
